planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring into sharply-drained sandy soil; in zone 9-10 plant February-April. Deep taproot resists transplanting once established, so choose a permanent, sunny, sandy site.

directions: Plant in full sun in lean, dry, extremely well-drained sandy soil; Feay's milkweed produces slender clusters of white flowers tinged with pink from March through August. It is endemic to Florida, growing naturally in open sandhills and scrubby flatwoods in association with wiregrass. Like all milkweeds it is a larval host plant for monarch caterpillars, and its drought tolerance makes it a good fit for xeric Florida native gardens where wetter milkweed species would struggle.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Gardening Solutions

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in moist, sandy, nutrient-poor soil in full sun in spring. One of the smallest milkweed species and easily overtopped by companion plants, so give it an open, low-competition site.

directions: Plant in full sun in consistently moist to seasonally wet, sandy, nutrient-poor soil; savannah milkweed is one of the smallest North American milkweeds, forming a diminutive clump with loose clusters of small greenish-yellow flowers from late spring through summer. It is native to wet pine savannas and flatwoods of the southeastern Coastal Plain from North Carolina to Florida, habitats that stay consistently damp but rarely flood deeply. It serves as a larval host plant for monarch, queen, and soldier butterflies and is a good fit for wet, sunny native plantings that mimic longleaf pine savanna conditions.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Gardening Solutions

planting.note: Plant in lean, dry, well-drained sandy soil in full sun in spring; winter dormant, emerging late, so mark its location to avoid disturbing the dormant crown.

directions: Plant in full sun in dry, lean, very well-drained sandy soil; velvetleaf milkweed is named for its densely hairy, soft-textured gray-green leaves, and it bears terminal clusters of pale, yellow-green flowers through the summer. It is native to sandy upland habitats of the southeastern Coastal Plain from the Carolinas south to Florida, with a disjunct population in eastern Texas. This robust, drought-tolerant species is an excellent monarch host plant for dry, sandy sites where showier milkweeds fail.

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in rocky, extremely well-drained soil in full sun in spring after frost danger passes; protect from prolonged temperatures below the low 20s F.

directions: Plant in full sun in rocky, gravelly, extremely well-drained desert soil; whitestem milkweed is an erect, nearly leafless shrub with slender, sticklike, waxy gray-green stems that give it a distinctive year-round architectural form. It is native to rocky, north-facing slopes of the Mojave and Sonoran Deserts in California, Arizona, and Baja California. It is a larval host plant for both monarch and queen butterflies and is exceptionally drought tolerant once established, making it a striking choice for desert and xeric gardens.

planting.note: Direct sow in fall for natural cold stratification, or stratify seed cold for 30 days before spring sowing, into lean, well-drained calcareous soil in full sun.

directions: Plant in full sun in lean, dry, well-drained soil, ideally with a calcareous or limestone component; slimleaf milkweed has fine, narrow, grass-like leaves and produces clusters of white flowers in summer. It is native to dry calcareous prairies and limestone glades across the Great Plains and Midwest, from Illinois and Montana south to Texas and New Mexico. It is a larval host plant for monarch butterflies and, though less common in the nursery trade, is well suited to lean prairie restorations.

planting.note: Direct sow in fall for natural cold stratification into lean, dry, well-drained prairie soil in full sun; grows from a taproot or slender rhizome and resents disturbance once established.

directions: Plant in full sun in lean, dry, well-drained prairie soil; plains milkweed is a dwarf species, usually only 8 to 10 inches tall, with tightly spiraled, thread-like leaves. It is native to short- and mixed-grass prairie of the northern and central Great Plains, from Montana south to the Texas panhandle. It is a larval host for monarch caterpillars and several moth species, and its flowers are also visited by native bees including the endangered rusty-patched bumble bee, making it valuable for lean, dry prairie plantings.

planting.note: Direct sow in fall for natural cold stratification into average, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; among the most cold-hardy milkweeds, suited to northern prairie and woodland-edge gardens.

directions: Plant in full sun to light shade in average, well-drained soil; oval-leaf milkweed has soft, rounded leaves and produces compact clusters of white to pale pink flowers tinged with purple from May into summer. It is native to open woodlands, prairies, and fields ranging from the Canadian prairie provinces of Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba south to Wyoming, Nebraska, and the western Great Lakes region, making it one of the hardiest native milkweeds for cold-climate gardens. It serves as a larval host for monarch caterpillars and is visited by early-season native bees.

planting.note: Plant in dry, sandy or gravelly, sharply-drained soil in full sun in spring; this very low, near-stemless milkweed is easy to overlook, so mark its location.

directions: Plant in full sun in dry, sandy, sharply-drained soil; dwarf milkweed is a very low-growing, near-stemless species with clusters of white, green, or pale yellow flowers held close to the ground from spring into early summer. It is native to dry plains, sandy desert scrub, grasslands, mesas, and open woodlands of the southwestern Great Plains and Southwest, occurring in Arizona, Colorado, Kansas, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Texas, and Utah at moderate elevations. It is a larval host plant for monarch and queen butterflies and needs minimal supplemental water once established.
sources: Idaho Fish and Game Species Catalog

planting.note: Plant in rocky or sandy, sharply-drained soil in full sun in spring; tolerates the sprawling, lax habit typical of desert wash species by giving it room to spread.

directions: Plant in full sun in rocky or sandy, sharply-drained soil; Mojave milkweed has thick, oval to lance-shaped leaves and produces dense, rounded umbels of pale green flowers tinged with pink in spring, on stems that often bend or sprawl rather than stand fully erect. It is native to desert washes, dry slopes, and scrubland of the Mojave and Sonoran Deserts from California to New Mexico. It is a larval host plant for monarch butterflies and is well suited to low-water desert gardens once established.
